criterion_notes.c1: Fails Criterion 1: the paper examines utility- and state-level non-revenue water (NRW) management and water-loss reduction (physical leakage, commercial losses, utility asset financing, and WSP technical staff capacity) in Peninsular Malaysia, rather than household or community water or sanitation service access.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 reading: Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, this study passes because it examines legal, regulatory, institutional, and governance reforms under Malaysia's Water Services Industry Act (WSIA) 2006 and SPAN Act 2006 (centralised regulation under NWSC, corporatisation/privatisation of state WSPs, transfer of water assets to PAAB, federal tariff-review authority, and licence-renewal KPIs). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, it fails Criterion 2 because although utility ownership/regulatory structure, licensing enforcement, and tariff/cost-recovery rules are rule-type mechanisms in form, in this study they are analysed solely as systemic incentives for utility NRW loss reduction and infrastructure capital financing rather than mechanisms directly governing household or community service access. Under both readings, the overall screening decision is exclude because Criteria 1 and 4 are not met.
criterion_notes.c3: Meets Criterion 3: contains primary qualitative empirical data from 19 in-depth stakeholder interviews (7 federal officials, 10 WSP senior staff/engineers, 2 NGO representatives) analysed via content analysis alongside secondary state-level NRW data to construct causal loop diagrams.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4: the only empirical outcomes reported are state/utility NRW rates (% of produced water lost/unbilled) and WSP operational/staff capacity for NRW reduction. Brief background mentions of low domestic tariffs and Selangor's free-water policy are discussed strictly as political constraints on WSP cost recovery and infrastructure investment, with no empirical outcome reported for household access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion.
criterion_notes.c5: Meets Criterion 5 for the study's own scope: unit of analysis (Peninsular Malaysia state WSPs and sector stakeholders), exposure (2006 WSIA/SPAN water sector restructuring), outcome (NRW reduction and WSP capacity), and qualitative systems-thinking study design are clearly identifiable.
criterion_notes.c6: Meets Criterion 6: full text is in English.

evidence_quotes.quote: This paper explores the challenges of water sector reform and NRW reduction in Malaysia to identify possible drivers that can accelerate the NRW management reform.
seven federal government officials, 10 senior staff or engineers from WSPs in different Malaysian states, and two non-governmental organisation (NGOs) representatives.
These reforms began with the adoption of two new water policy instruments: the Water Services Industry Act (WSIA) 2006 and the National Water Services Industry Act (SPAN Act) 2006.
Finally, the reforms aim to create a strong incentive for WSPs to pursue NRW reduction by tying licence renewal to NRW rates.

By the end of 2016, the first three states to sign and complete the water restructuring exercises – Melaka, Johor, and Negeri Sembilan – achieved substantial reductions in NRW rates (Table S3, available online).

raw_response.exposure: 2006 Malaysian water supply sector regulatory and financing reforms (Water Services Industry Act 2006 and SPAN Act 2006: federal regulation under NWSC, WSP corporatisation/privatisation, PAAB asset-light financing model, federal tariff-setting authority, and licence renewal tied to NRW targets)
raw_response.outcome: State and water service provider (WSP) non-revenue water (NRW) rates (%) and WSP operational/human-resource capacity for NRW reduction
raw_response.population_and_sample: State water service providers (WSPs) across Peninsular Malaysia (11 states, excluding Sabah and Sarawak) and 19 interviewed stakeholders (7 federal government officials, 10 senior WSP staff or engineers, and 2 NGO representatives)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded (E01 - Wrong topic; also lacks any eligible access outcome under Criterion 4). Using 19 stakeholder interviews, secondary NRW statistics, and causal loop diagrams, the paper analyses Malaysia's 2006 water sector regulatory and financing reforms (WSIA 2006, SPAN Act 2006, WSP corporatisation, PAAB asset ownership, tariff-review centralisation, and licensing KPIs) solely in relation to utility non-revenue water (NRW) loss reduction and WSP technical capacity. It does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access (c1 = no) and reports no empirical outcome on household access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion (c4 = no). Therefore, it is excluded under both the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading and the plain wording of Criterion 2.
raw_response.study_design: Qualitative empirical study using semi-structured stakeholder interviews with content analysis, secondary NRW statistics/document review, and systems thinking causal loop diagrams (CLDs)
